Key manipulation methods include [table\.py L402](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L402) for general field updates, [templates\.py L610](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L610) and [structure\.py L1637](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L1637) for creating subsets based on predicates, and [structure\.py L942](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L942) or [structure\.py L958](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L958) for generating simplified views of the structure\.

 The data model is supported by a comprehensive parsing pipeline\. The [input\.md?plain=1 L909](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L909) module \(in [`src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py)\) enables the creation of [structure\.py L306](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) objects from diverse inputs, including mmCIF files, raw atom arrays, and sequence data\. This module also handles common data inconsistencies and applies fixes, such as resolving alternative locations and reordering specific atoms, ensuring a standardized representation for downstream processing\. The system also supports detailed chemical component information, including atoms and bonds, through the [run\_alphafold\.py L50](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold.py#L50) module \(in [`src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py)\), which can parse and manage data from the Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\)\.

 The C\+\+ backend, located in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp), provides high\-performance implementations for tasks such as [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) parsing, alternative location resolution, and bond extraction\. These C\+\+ components are exposed to Python via [README\.md?plain=1 L148](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/README.md?plain=1#L148) and significantly enhance the efficiency of structural data processing within the [structure\.py L306](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) data model\.### High\-Performance C\+\+ `mmCIF` Processing and Numerical Operations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold 3 model incorporates a high\-performance C\+\+ backend, exposed to Python through [README\.md?plain=1 L148](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/README.md?plain=1#L148), to efficiently process and manipulate [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) \(macromolecular Crystallographic Information File\) data\. This backend is crucial for handling large structural datasets, performing tasks such as [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) parsing, alternative location resolution, atom site filtering, residue fixing, bond extraction, and optimizing NumPy array operations\.

 Core to this functionality is the [mmcif\_layout\.h L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h#L37) class, implemented in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_lib.cc)\. This class manages the structural hierarchy of a parsed [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) file, providing indexed access to chains, residues, and atoms within a specific model\. It allows for efficient querying of atom, residue, and chain ranges, and supports filtering to retain only a subset of residues or atoms\. The [mmcif\_layout\.h L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h#L37) is capable of processing multi\-model [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) files and distinguishing between [parsing\.py L1118](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L1118) and [parsing\.py L1120](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L1120) for robust residue identification\.

 The system includes robust mechanisms for resolving alternative atom locations \(alt\-locs\)\. The [mmcif\_altlocs\.h L49](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.h#L49) function, detailed in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.cc), intelligently selects the most appropriate atom representation for alt\-loc groups based on occupancy and alphabetical tie\-breaking rules\. This process handles both partial and whole residue alt\-loc scenarios, simplifying structural data by providing a single, consistent representation\.

 For atom site processing, utility functions exposed through [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_atom_site_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_atom_site_pybind.cc) infer atom type symbols when not explicitly provided and map internal chain IDs to author chain IDs for consistency\. This ensures accurate interpretation of atomic properties and chain assignments\.

 The C\+\+ backend also performs targeted structural corrections\. For instance, the [mmcif\_utils\_pybind\.cc L438](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_utils_pybind.cc#L438) function, part of the utilities in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_utils_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_utils_pybind.cc), can reorder specific atoms in residues, such as Arginine, to ensure consistent atom ordering in structural analyses\. This also includes generating boolean masks for polymer and ligand residues, helping to align residue selections across various [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) tables\.

 Bond information extraction is another key function\. The [mmcif\_struct\_conn\.h L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn.h#L37) function, implemented in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_lib.cc), determines atom indices involved in bonds from [mmcif\.py L144](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L144) and [mmcif\.py L140](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L140) tables\. It accounts for different [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) column conventions and validates data consistency, addressing irregularities common in PDB data\.

 Beyond structural parsing, the C\+\+ components also provide optimized numerical operations for NumPy arrays\. As shown in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc), this includes remapping elements in object arrays, efficiently formatting float arrays to strings, and performing fast [membership\.pyi L23](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership.pyi#L23) checks for object arrays, which significantly outperforms Python\-native NumPy operations for these specific tasks by leveraging C\+\+'s performance\. Efficient grouping of indices by value is also provided via [aggregation\_pybind\.cc L34](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/aggregation_pybind.cc#L34) in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/aggregation_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/aggregation_pybind.cc), along with optimized membership checking for [cif\_dict\_pybind\.cc L177](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L177) NumPy arrays as detailed in [`src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.cc)\.

 All these C\+\+ functionalities are integrated with Python using [README\.md?plain=1 L148](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/README.md?plain=1#L148), employing [cif\_dict\_pybind\.cc L393](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L393) to free the Python Global Interpreter Lock \(GIL\) during computationally intensive C\+\+ operations, thereby enhancing concurrency and overall application responsiveness\. The use of [mkdssp\_pybind\.cc L44](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/mkdssp_pybind.cc#L44) and [CMakeLists\.txt L91](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/CMakeLists.txt#L91) further contributes to efficiency by minimizing string copying and enabling fast hash\-based lookups\.### JAX\-Based 3D Geometry Utilities with Struct\-of\-Arrays

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold 3 leverages JAX for high\-performance numerical computations, including a suite of 3D geometry utilities designed for efficient batch processing and integration with JAX's auto\-differentiation capabilities\. These utilities are built upon a "Struct of Arrays" \(SoA\) pattern, which optimizes data layout for parallel processing on accelerators like TPUs and GPUs, improving both performance and numerical precision by storing components \([vector\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L51), [vector\.py L52](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L52), [vector\.py L53](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L53) for vectors, or matrix elements for rotations\) as separate arrays rather than bundling them into an array of structures\. This approach is implemented through the [struct\_of\_array\.py L199](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py#L199) decorator, found in [`src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py), which transforms standard dataclasses into JAX\-compatible pytree nodes with array\-like behaviors such as slicing and shape/dtype validation\.

 The core geometric primitives include:

 - **[vector\.py L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) for 3D Vectors**: Defined in [`src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py), the [vector\.py L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class represents collections of 3D vectors\. It supports fundamental vector arithmetic \(addition, subtraction, scaling, dot products, cross products\) and geometric calculations such as norms and normalization\. These operations are overloaded to work intuitively with other [vector\.py L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) instances or scalars, and are mapped across the array components using [run\_alphafold\.py L495](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold.py#L495) for efficiency\. Utility functions also extend to calculating squared Euclidean distances, Euclidean distances, and dihedral angles\.
- **[rotation\_matrix\.py L118](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) for Rotation Matrices**: The [rotation\_matrix\.py L118](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) class, located in [`src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py), provides a JAX\-compatible representation for 3x3 rotation matrices\. It facilitates operations such as inversion \(transposition\), applying rotations to points, and composing rotations\. [rotation\_matrix\.py L118](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) instances can be constructed from various inputs, including two vectors, quaternions, or through Singular Value Decomposition \(SVD\), with specific implementations designed for numerical stability and differentiability within JAX\. The class also supports the generation of uniform random rotations\.
- **[rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L109](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) for Rigid Transformations**: Combining rotations and translations, the [rigid\_matrix\_vector\.py L109](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) class in [`src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py) encapsulates 3D rigid transformations\. It enables operations like composition of transformations, inversion, and applying transformations to 3D points\. A key feature is its ability to compute the optimal rigid transformation required to align one set of 3D points to another, utilizing a weighted least\-squares approach and SVD to derive the rotation\.

 These utilities are centrally accessible through [`src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/__init__.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/__init__.py), which re\-exports the main classes and functions, simplifying their integration into AlphaFold 3's larger computational graph\. Additional geometric utility functions, such as [utils\.py L28](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/utils.py#L28) for array manipulation and [utils\.py L35](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/utils.py#L35) for angular differences, are provided in [`src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/utils.py)\.## Core Utilities and Constants

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Foundational utilities and data structures support AlphaFold 3, encompassing configuration management, input data representation and parsing, secure deserialization, and resource access\. This includes comprehensive constants and utility functions for molecular biology data such as atom types, chemical component definitions, residue names, periodic table data, and side chain torsion angles\.

 Configuration objects are managed through a system that automatically converts classes into [run\_alphafold\.py L543](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold.py#L543) instances, enabling type coercion for nested configurations\. This allows for configurations to be defined using standard Python dictionaries and then automatically transformed into the appropriate configuration objects\. The system also supports defining default factories for fields using an [base\_config\.py L52](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py#L52) mechanism\. This functionality is primarily defined by the [base\_config\.py L137](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py#L137) class and its metaclass, [base\_config\.py L74](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py#L74), located in [`src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py)\.

 The input data for AlphaFold 3 models, which can include proteins, RNA, DNA chains, and ligands, is managed by a dedicated system that represents and validates this data\. This system facilitates reading input from various formats, including custom JSON formats and mmCIF, and handles file compression\. It converts these external formats into a standardized internal representation using the [folding\_input\.py L951](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L951) dataclass\. Key components include chain\-specific classes like [folding\_input\.py L137](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L137), [folding\_input\.py L457](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L457), [folding\_input\.py L666](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L666), and [folding\_input\.py L809](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L809), each with validation logic and methods for conversion between internal objects and JSON representations\. The [folding\_input\.py L98](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L98) class represents structural templates used for protein chains\. The utility function [folding\_input\.py L59](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L59) in [`src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py) handles the reading of potentially compressed external files for large data such as MSAs and templates\.

 Secure deserialization of Python objects from trusted [run\_alphafold\_test\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_test.py#L29) data is implemented to mitigate security risks\. This is achieved by restricting the types of objects that can be loaded to an allowlist of built\-in Python types\. The [safe\_pickle\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) class, defined in [`src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py), overrides the [safe\_pickle\.py L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L54) method of [safe\_pickle\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) to enforce this allowlist, raising an [safe\_pickle\.py L26](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L26) for any unpermitted types\.

 Access to external data files and resources is managed through utilities that locate and access these resources relative to the package root\. The module [`src/alphafold3/common/resources.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/resources.py) defines a root directory for resources and provides functions to construct paths, open files, and traverse resource directories, leveraging [run\_alphafold\_data\_test\.py L275](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L275) for robust path manipulation\.

 The codebase includes a comprehensive set of constants and utility functions for molecular biology data\. Atom types for proteins and nucleic acids are defined, along with mappings for residue\-specific atom lists and structured representations for fixed\-size data storage\. This includes various atom representations like [atom\_types\.py L143](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L143) and [atom\_types\.py L154](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L154) for proteins, and [atom\_types\.py L191](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L191) for both protein and nucleic acid residues, all specified in [`src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py)\.

 Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) data is managed through a structured interface that allows access to chemical component information\. The [chemical\_components\.py L46](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L46) class in [`src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py) provides a read\-only wrapper around a dictionary of chemical components, loading data from pickle files and supporting user\-defined overrides\. [chemical\_components\.py L117](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L117) dataclasses represent extracted information for single chemical components\. Tools for converting CCD CIF files to Python pickles and for generating sets of specific chemical components \(glycans, ions\) are located in [`src/alphafold3/constants/converters`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/converters)\. The identified sets of chemical components are stored in [`src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py)\.

 Constants related to mmCIF data structures and utility functions for classifying and standardizing residue and chain types are provided to parse and interpret molecular structure data\. This includes definitions for various chain types \(e\.g\., [mmcif\_names\.py L48](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py#L48), [mmcif\_names\.py L41](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py#L41)\) and functions to infer polymer types based on residue sequences, as detailed in [`src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py)\.

 A comprehensive periodic table of elements, including properties like name, number, symbol, and weight, is defined in [`src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py)\. This data is represented using an [periodic\_table\.py L30](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py#L30) dataclass and provides mappings for atomic numbers and weights, including an unknown element [periodic\_table\.py L42](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py#L42) for flexibility\.

 Mappings and constant definitions for three\-letter and one\-letter residue names are central to handling biomolecular structures\. This includes standard and modified amino acids, as well as nucleic acids\. These definitions facilitate conversion between naming conventions and categorize residues for various biological contexts, leveraging [atom\_types\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L29) for string optimization\. This is found in [`src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py)\.

 Finally, constants related to amino acid side chain torsion \(chi\) angles are defined, including the specific atoms that form these angles for each residue type\. These definitions provide utility mappings and masks for fixed\-length chi angle arrays, enabling consistent handling of side\-chain conformations\. This information is available in [`src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py)\.### Input Data Representation and Parsing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold 3 model utilizes a structured approach for representing and parsing diverse input data, centralizing this functionality within the [folding\_input\.py L951](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L951) dataclass found in [`src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py)\. This class serves as a comprehensive container for all macromolecular entities, including proteins, RNAs, DNAs, and ligands, along with associated metadata necessary for model prediction\.

 The [folding\_input\.py L951](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L951) dataclass supports loading data from various sources\. It can parse input from the AlphaFold Server JSON format through its [folding\_input\.py L1038](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1038) method, or from the AlphaFold 3 JSON format using the [folding\_input\.py L1127](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1127) method, which is capable of handling external file references for large data elements like Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), mmCIF files, and user\-defined Chemical Component Dictionaries \(CCDs\)\. Additionally, it can directly parse mmCIF strings into its internal representation via [parsing\.py L408](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L408)\.

 Chain\-specific components, such as [folding\_input\.py L137](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L137), [folding\_input\.py L457](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L457), [folding\_input\.py L666](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L666), and [folding\_input\.py L809](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L809), manage the unique attributes and validations for each molecular type\. For instance, [folding\_input\.py L137](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L137) stores information about sequences, post\-translational modifications, and associated MSAs and structural templates, while [folding\_input\.py L809](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L809) handles SMILES strings or CCD identifiers for small molecules\. These chain objects also provide mechanisms for converting their internal state to various external formats and for validating their content upon initialization\.

 Once the input data is loaded into the [folding\_input\.py L951](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L951) object, it can be seamlessly converted into a [run\_alphafold\_data\_test\.py L88](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) object using the [folding\_input\.py L1389](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1389) method\. This [run\_alphafold\_data\_test\.py L88](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) object, as detailed in [Immutable Molecular Structure Data Model](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3#molecular-structure-representation-and-manipulation-immutable-molecular-structure-data-model), is AlphaFold 3's immutable, typed, NumPy array\-backed data model for molecular structures, facilitating downstream structural analysis and manipulation\. This structured approach ensures that diverse biological inputs are consistently processed and made ready for the model's prediction pipeline\.### Secure Deserialization with Restricted Unpickler

```
# Allowed built-in types for safe unpickling.
_ALLOWED_BUILTINS = frozenset({
    "NoneType", "bool", "bytes", "dict", "float", "frozenset", "int", "list",
    "set", "str", "tuple",
})

class _RestrictedUnpickler(pickle.Unpickler):
  """A pickle `Unpickler` that forbids loading arbitrary global classes."""

  def find_class(self, module: str, name: str) -> Any:
    """Returns the class for `module` and `name` if allowed."""
    if module == "builtins" and name in _ALLOWED_BUILTINS:
      return super().find_class(module, name)
    raise pickle.UnpicklingError(f"Can't unpickle disallowed '{module}.{name}'")

# The `load` function (not shown) uses this unpickler for safe deserialization.
```

The [run\_alphafold\_test\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_test.py#L29) module in Python is a powerful tool for serializing and deserializing Python object structures\. However, deserializing data from untrusted sources using [run\_alphafold\_test\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_test.py#L29) can pose a significant security risk, as a malicious actor could embed arbitrary code that executes upon unpickling\. To mitigate this vulnerability, AlphaFold 3 incorporates a secure deserialization mechanism to process [run\_alphafold\_test\.py L29](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_test.py#L29) data safely\.

 This mechanism is primarily implemented by the [safe\_pickle\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) class, which extends the standard [safe\_pickle\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51)\. The core of its security lies in overriding the [safe\_pickle\.py L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L54) method, which is responsible for locating and importing classes during the deserialization process\. Instead of allowing any class to be instantiated, [safe\_pickle\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) enforces a strict allowlist\. It permits the instantiation of classes only if they originate from the [safe\_pickle\.py L56](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L56) module and their names are explicitly present in a predefined set of innocuous types\. Any attempt to unpickle a class that falls outside these stringent criteria results in a [safe\_pickle\.py L58](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L58), effectively preventing the creation of potentially harmful objects\.

 The [safe\_pickle\.py L36](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L36) frozenset defines this allowlist, containing fundamental Python types such as [base\_config\.py L37](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py#L37), [run\_alphafold\.py L436](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold.py#L436), [run\_alphafold\_data\_test\.py L71](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L71), [cif\_dict\_lib\.h L125](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h#L125), [vector\.py L32](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L32), [features\.py L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L54), [input\.md?plain=1 L142](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L142), [README\.md?plain=1 L75](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/README.md?plain=1#L75), [README\.md?plain=1 L22](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/README.md?plain=1#L22), [input\.md?plain=1 L140](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L140), and [run\_alphafold\.py L1064](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold.py#L1064)\. This ensures that only basic and inherently safe data structures can be reconstructed from serialized data\.

 The public [safe\_pickle\.py L61](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L61) function serves as the primary interface for this secure unpickling\. It instantiates [safe\_pickle\.py L51](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) with the provided file\-like object and then uses it to deserialize data, ensuring that all loaded objects adhere to the enforced type restrictions\. This safeguard is crucial for maintaining the integrity and security of AlphaFold 3, especially when dealing with serialized data that might originate from external or potentially tampered sources\. This functionality is defined within [`src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py)\.### Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) Management and Conversion

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold 3 manages and accesses the Chemical Components Dictionary \(CCD\) to process detailed information about chemical components found in macromolecular structures, such as small molecules, ligands, and modified residues\. This data is critical for correctly interpreting molecular structures and for feature generation in the model\.

 The system utilizes the [chemical\_components\.py L46](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L46) class in [`src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py), which acts as a read\-only interface to the CCD data\. This class efficiently loads pre\-processed CCD information from a pickled file and allows for additional user\-defined CCD entries, ensuring flexibility and preventing accidental modification of the core data\. Details about individual chemical components are encapsulated in the [chemical\_components\.py L117](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L117) dataclass, which stores attributes like name, type, SMILES strings, and formula weight\. The [chemical\_components\.py L183](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L183) function provides a cached mechanism to retrieve this information for a given residue name, optimizing lookup performance\.

 To prepare the CCD for efficient use, AlphaFold 3 includes conversion scripts\. The script [`src/alphafold3/constants/converters/ccd_pickle_gen.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/ccd_pickle_gen.py) converts raw [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) or gzipped [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) CCD files into a Python pickle format, which can then be loaded quickly by the [chemical\_components\.py L46](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L46) class\. Another script, [`src/alphafold3/constants/converters/chemical_component_sets_gen.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/chemical_component_sets_gen.py), processes this pickled CCD data to identify and categorize specific sets of chemical components, such as glycans \(linking and non\-linking\) and ions\. This categorization is useful for downstream analysis and specific model features, enabling the system to differentiate between biologically relevant components and those related to experimental conditions, like common crystallization aids\. These categorized sets are stored as immutable [features\.py L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L54) objects for efficient access, as described in [`src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py)\.### Molecular Biology Constants and Mappings

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold 3 includes a comprehensive set of constants and mappings essential for handling molecular biology data, providing standardized representations for various aspects of molecular structures\. These definitions are crucial for consistent data processing and model input generation, encompassing atom types, residue naming conventions, periodic table data, and side chain torsion angles\.

 Atom type definitions are centralized in [`src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py)\. This includes global string constants for common atom names, mappings of residue names to their constituent atoms \(excluding hydrogens\), and specific definitions for protein backbone atoms\. To facilitate fixed\-size array representations for machine learning models, various atom sets are defined, such as [atom\_types\.py L143](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L143) for a comprehensive 37\-atom protein representation, [atom\_types\.py L154](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L154) for a more compact 14\-atom protein representation, and [atom\_types\.py L191](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L191) for a general\-purpose dense atom representation covering both proteins and nucleic acids\. These structured atom definitions ensure consistent input dimensions for neural network architectures\.

 Residue naming conventions and classifications are managed in [`src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py)\. This file provides extensive mappings, including [residue\_names\.py L28](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py#L28), which converts three\-letter residue codes \(from the Chemical Components Dictionary\) to their one\-letter equivalents\. It also categorizes residues into various tuples like [residue\_names\.py L278](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py#L278), [residue\_names\.py L356](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py#L356), [residue\_names\.py L357](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py#L357), and [residue\_names\.py L390](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py#L390) to support different biological contexts and enable flexible data handling\. Integer mappings of residue names further assist in numerical representation for computational tasks\. Building upon these, [`src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py) defines constants related to [input\.md?plain=1 L38](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/input.md?plain=1#L38) data structures and provides utility functions to classify and standardize residue and chain types\. This includes inferring polymer types \(protein, DNA, RNA\) based on residue sequences and converting non\-standard residue names to their closest standard equivalents, which is vital for processing diverse structural data\.

 The system also integrates data from the Chemical Components Dictionary \(CCD\)\. The [`src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py) file provides a structured interface for accessing CCD information, including details such as component names, types, and SMILES strings\. This is complemented by [`src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py), which loads predefined sets of chemical components, categorizing them into glycans and common crystallization aids for specialized handling\. Tools for converting raw CCD CIF files into a more efficient pickled format are located in [`src/alphafold3/constants/converters/ccd_pickle_gen.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/ccd_pickle_gen.py), and for generating categorized sets of chemical components from these pickled files in [`src/alphafold3/constants/converters/chemical_component_sets_gen.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/chemical_component_sets_gen.py)\.

 Periodic table data, including elemental names, atomic numbers, symbols, and weights, is defined in [`src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py)\. This provides a foundational set of chemical properties for all elements, including an "Unknown" element \([periodic\_table\.py L42](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py#L42)\) to accommodate cases where specific elemental information might be absent in the input data\.

 Finally, amino acid side chain torsion angles \(chi angles\) are detailed in [`src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py)\. This file maps 3\-letter amino acid codes to the specific atoms that define each chi angle, enabling accurate conformational analysis\. It also provides derived constants, such as [side\_chains\.py L84](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py#L84) and [side\_chains\.py L99](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py#L99), to manage the variable number of chi angles across different amino acids, ensuring consistent data representation for downstream calculations\.## Model Output Scoring and Validation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The AlphaFold 3 model incorporates a suite of methods for evaluating and validating the quality of its predicted molecular structures\. These methods encompass structural alignment, quantification of differences using Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\), characterization of ligand chirality, and the generation of simplified structural representations known as pseudo\-beta atom positions\.

 Structural alignment and RMSD calculations are foundational for comparing a predicted structure against a known reference\. The functionality found in [`src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py) provides tools to rigorously align 3D coordinate sets and quantify the deviations between them\. This includes [alignment\.py L25](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py#L25), which determines the optimal rigid transformation \(rotation and translation\) to superimpose one set of coordinates onto another, and [hmmalign\.py L68](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L68), which applies this transformation\. Based on these alignments, [alignment\.py L105](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py#L105) computes atom\-specific distances, and [alignment\.py L134](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py#L134) aggregates these distances into a single RMSD value, offering a quantitative measure of structural similarity\.

 Beyond overall structural similarity, AlphaFold 3 also includes specific mechanisms for validating ligand stereochemistry\. The functionality in [`src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py) is dedicated to detecting and comparing chiral centers within ligands\. This module can convert AlphaFold 3's internal [run\_alphafold\_data\_test\.py L88](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects into RDKit molecules, identify chiral centers, and compare their configurations against reference molecules, which can be provided explicitly or sourced from the Chemical Components Dictionary \(CCD\)\. This process is crucial for ensuring that predicted ligand poses maintain the correct stereochemistry\.

 For simplified structural representations, the [scoring\.py L30](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py#L30) function in [`src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py) generates pseudo\-beta atom positions\. This function abstracts full atomic coordinates into a single point per residue or ligand, which can be valuable for coarse\-grained analysis or as input for certain scoring metrics\. These pseudo\-beta positions are derived from the amino acid type and full atom coordinates, with special handling for ligands to ensure their inclusion in this simplified representation\.### Ligand Chirality Detection and Comparison

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Ligand chirality detection and comparison is critical for validating the stereochemical accuracy of predicted ligand structures\. AlphaFold 3 employs a process that identifies chiral centers, converts structural data into RDKit molecules, and then compares the stereochemistry against reference structures\. The [chirality\.py L58](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L58) function, found in [`src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py), is central to this process\. It determines if a ligand's predicted chiral centers and their assigned chirality align with those of a reference molecule\.

 The comparison begins by converting the structural representation of a ligand into an RDKit molecule, which facilitates the use of established cheminformatics tools\. Functions such as [chirality\.py L44](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L44) are used to identify chiral atoms within these RDKit molecules, focusing on common chiral elements such as carbon and sulfur\. Stereochemistry is assigned to these RDKit molecules based on their 3D coordinates using [rdkit\_utils\.py L157](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L157)\.

 For each ligand in a predicted structure, a reference molecule is obtained, either from a provided mapping or by querying the Chemical Components Dictionary \(CCD\)\. The core comparison logic in [chirality\.py L58](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L58) then verifies if the ligand's atoms are a subset of the reference molecule's atoms and if their respective chiral centers and stereochemical assignments are consistent\. This approach allows for flexibility, accommodating scenarios where a predicted ligand structure might be incomplete compared to its canonical reference\. For further details on the molecular structure representation, see [Immutable Molecular Structure Data Model](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3#molecular-structure-representation-and-manipulation-immutable-molecular-structure-data-model)\.## Deployment and Execution Environment

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

AlphaFold 3 is packaged and deployed using Docker, which containerizes the application and its dependencies into a self\-contained environment\. This approach ensures reproducibility and simplifies deployment across various computing infrastructures\. The Docker build process, defined in the [performance\.md?plain=1 L300](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/performance.md?plain=1#L300) at [`docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile), starts with an NVIDIA CUDA base image, reflecting the model's reliance on GPU acceleration\.

 The containerization process includes installing necessary system\-level dependencies for Python execution and compiling core components\. A key part of this setup is the integration of HMMER, a suite of bioinformatics tools\. HMMER is downloaded, a custom patch is applied to modify its behavior, and then it is compiled and installed within the Docker image\. This ensures that the specific version and configuration of HMMER required by AlphaFold 3 are consistently available\.

 Python dependencies are managed using [pyproject\.toml L42](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/pyproject.toml#L42), a package installer configured for efficient and reproducible virtual environment management\. This setup helps to isolate AlphaFold 3's Python environment, preventing conflicts with other software\. The build process also includes a step to generate essential chemical components data\.

 To optimize performance, particularly for large models, specific XLA \(Accelerated Linear Algebra\) flags are set within the Docker environment\. These flags address known XLA issues and manage memory allocation for JAX operations, which is crucial for efficient execution of AlphaFold 3's neural network computations\.### AlphaFold 3 Docker Containerization

```
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.6.3-base-ubuntu24.04

# Install Python, Git, compilers, and libraries.
RUN DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    apt-get update --quiet \
    && apt-get install --yes --quiet python3.12 python3.12-dev git wget gcc g++ make zlib1g-dev zstd

# Install uv for dependency management.
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.9.24 /uv /uvx /bin/
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1
ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/alphafold3_venv
RUN uv venv $UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT

ENV PATH="/hmmer/bin:/alphafold3_venv/bin:$PATH"

# Install HMMER from source, applying a patch.
# (Full HMMER installation steps are omitted for brevity, see Dockerfile)
RUN mkdir /hmmer_build /hmmer ; \
    wget http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/hmmer-3.4.tar.gz --directory-prefix /hmmer_build ; \
    # ... further HMMER build steps ...
    rm -R /hmmer_build

# Copy AlphaFold 3 source and set working directory.
COPY . /app/alphafold
WORKDIR /app/alphafold

# Install AlphaFold 3 dependencies using uv.
ARG UV_EXTRAS=""
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    UV_LINK_MODE=copy uv sync --frozen --all-groups --no-editable $UV_EXTRAS

# Build chemical components database.
RUN uv run build_data

# Performance-critical XLA environment variables.
ENV XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false"
ENV XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=true
ENV XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95

CMD ["uv", "run", "python3", "run_alphafold.py"]
```

The AlphaFold 3 Docker image is constructed to provide a self\-contained environment for running the model, ensuring consistent execution across different systems\. The build process, defined by the [performance\.md?plain=1 L300](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/performance.md?plain=1#L300) at [`docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile), starts with an NVIDIA CUDA base image \([Dockerfile L20](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L20)\), which establishes the foundation for GPU acceleration\.

 System\-level dependencies, including Python, Git, and various compilers, are installed using [Dockerfile L28](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L28) to support the build and execution of AlphaFold 3 and its components\. Python environment management is handled by [pyproject\.toml L42](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/pyproject.toml#L42), which is configured to create isolated virtual environments and efficiently install dependencies\. This approach ensures reproducibility and manages Python packages effectively\.

 A crucial aspect of the Docker image is the integration of HMMER, a suite of bioinformatics tools\. Instead of relying on pre\-packaged versions, HMMER [Dockerfile L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L54) is downloaded, a custom patch \([Dockerfile L59](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L59)\) is applied, and the suite is compiled from source within the Docker build\. This allows for precise version control and specific modifications to HMMER's functionality, which are necessary for AlphaFold 3's data processing\. More details on how these external tools are managed can be found in [Bioinformatics Command\-Line Tool Wrappers](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3#data-processing-and-feature-engineering-bioinformatics-command-line-tool-wrappers)\.

 Performance optimization is a key consideration within the Docker environment\. XLA \(Accelerated Linear Algebra\) flags are set to disable Triton GEMM, addressing known XLA issues and ensuring efficient execution on NVIDIA GPUs\. Additionally, environment variables are configured to optimize memory usage, particularly for handling large models on high\-capacity GPUs\. These settings contribute to efficient tensor computation and overall model performance\. Further details on how AlphaFold 3 manages efficient computation are available in [Haiku Modules and Efficient Computation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3#alphafold-3-model-architecture-and-training-haiku-modules-and-efficient-computation)\.### HMMER Integration and Customization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

HMMER is integrated into the AlphaFold 3 Docker image through a multi\-step process that ensures a specific version is used and that it includes a custom patch\. This integration begins with downloading the [Dockerfile L54](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L54) archive from [Dockerfile L48](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L48) into the [Dockerfile L53](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L53) directory within the Docker image, as defined in [`docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile)\. A SHA256 checksum is performed on the downloaded archive to verify its integrity before proceeding\.

 A custom patch is then applied to the HMMER source code\. This patch introduces modifications to HMMER's behavior, indicating specific requirements for AlphaFold 3's usage of the tool\. After the patch is applied, HMMER is compiled and installed into [Dockerfile L42](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L42)\. This compilation process includes the [Dockerfile L66](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L66) library, which is a foundational component often used with HMMER for sequence analysis utilities\. This custom build and patching approach ensures that AlphaFold 3 operates with a precisely controlled HMMER environment, which is crucial for consistency in Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) generation and related bioinformatics tasks\. For more details on how these tools are utilized within AlphaFold 3's data processing pipeline, refer to [Bioinformatics Command\-Line Tool Wrappers](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3#data-processing-and-feature-engineering-bioinformatics-command-line-tool-wrappers)\.### XLA Performance Optimization

```
# To work around a known XLA issue causing the compilation time to greatly
# increase, the following environment variable setting XLA flags must be enabled
# when running AlphaFold 3. Note that if using CUDA capability 7 GPUs, it is
# necessary to set the following XLA_FLAGS value instead:
# ENV XLA_FLAGS="--xla_disable_hlo_passes=custom-kernel-fusion-rewriter"
# (no need to disable gemm in that case as it is not supported for such GPU).
ENV XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false"
# Memory settings used for folding up to 5,120 tokens on A100 80 GB.
ENV XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=true
ENV XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95

CMD ["uv", "run", "python3", "run_alphafold.py"]
```

The AlphaFold 3 Docker environment includes specific configurations for XLA \(Accelerated Linear Algebra\) to optimize performance and manage memory usage effectively during model execution\. These optimizations are crucial for handling the large computational demands of the AlphaFold 3 model\.

 One key optimization involves setting the [run\_alphafold\.py L957](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/run_alphafold.py#L957) environment variable to disable Triton GEMM \(General Matrix Multiply\)\. This addresses a known issue within XLA that can impact performance\. Additionally, [Dockerfile L95](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L95) and [Dockerfile L96](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile#L96) are configured to control how XLA manages GPU memory\. These settings are particularly important for large models, such as AlphaFold 3's capacity for up to 5,120 tokens, enabling efficient memory allocation on GPUs like the A100 80 GB\. These flags help prevent out\-of\-memory errors and ensure that the model can run efficiently within the available hardware constraints\. The specific XLA flags are defined within the [performance\.md?plain=1 L300](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/performance.md?plain=1#L300) at [`docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docker/Dockerfile)\.## Cloud Platform Utilities and Data Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This section outlines the utilities and scripts designed to manage large biological sequence datasets and local SSDs, primarily within the Google Cloud Platform \(GCP\) environment\. These tools facilitate large\-scale data operations and automation in a cloud context\.

 One script, located at [`src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh), automates the mounting of local SSDs on GCP instances, configuring them for persistent storage\. This process ensures that available local SSDs are identified, formatted, and mounted to a specified directory, providing efficient storage for data\-intensive tasks\. The script is designed to be idempotent, meaning it can be run multiple times without causing adverse effects, as it skips operations if the SSD is already configured or mounted\.

 Another script, located at [`src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh), handles the efficient copying of large biological sequence files to these local SSDs\. It prioritizes files to maximize the use of limited storage space, copying data in parallel\. This utility is particularly useful for managing extensive datasets often encountered in bioinformatics applications, ensuring that critical data is available on high\-speed local storage\. Files that cannot be accommodated due to space constraints are reported\.### GCP Local SSD Management and Mounting

```
# Iterates through local SSDs.
for SSD_DISK in $(realpath "$(find /dev/disk/by-id/ | grep google-local)")
do
  # Check if the disk is already formatted.
  if ! blkid -o value -s TYPE "${SSD_DISK}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Disk ${SSD_DISK} is not formatted, format it."
    mkfs.ext4 -m 0 -E lazy_itable_init=0,lazy_journal_init=0,discard "${SSD_DISK}" || continue
  fi

  # Checks if the disk is already mounted (stubbed for brevity).
  # The original script checks against '/proc/mounts'.
  # if grep -qs "^/dev/nvme0n1 " /proc/mounts; then
  #   echo "Disk ${SSD_DISK} is already mounted, skip it."
  #   continue
  # fi

  # Disk is not mounted, mount it.
  echo "Mounting ${SSD_DISK} to ${MOUNT_DIR}"
  mkdir -p "${MOUNT_DIR}" # MOUNT_DIR is defined at the top of the script.
  chmod -R 777 "${MOUNT_DIR}"
  mount "${SSD_DISK}" "${MOUNT_DIR}"
  break
done
```

The [`src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh) script automates the process of identifying, formatting, and mounting local SSDs on Google Cloud Platform instances\. This script is designed to be idempotent, meaning it can be run multiple times without causing unintended side effects; it will skip operations if an SSD is already mounted or if the target mount directory already exists\.

 The script locates local SSD devices by searching [gcp\_mount\_ssd\.sh L30](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L30) for entries matching [gcp\_mount\_ssd\.sh L30](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L30)\. For each identified SSD, it determines if the disk is already formatted using [gcp\_mount\_ssd\.sh L33](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L33)\. If not, it formats the disk with the [gcp\_mount\_ssd\.sh L35](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L35) filesystem, disabling lazy initialization and enabling discard\. It then checks [gcp\_mount\_ssd\.sh L39](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L39) to see if the disk is currently mounted\. If an unmounted SSD is found, the script creates the designated mount directory \(defaulting to [installation\.md?plain=1 L258](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/docs/installation.md?plain=1#L258)\), sets its permissions, and mounts the SSD to that directory\. The script prioritizes mounting the first available unmounted SSD it finds\. If no unmounted SSDs are located after checking all candidates, the script exits with an error\.### Parallel Data Copying to Local SSDs

```
# Iterates through files, checks available space, prunes the list if necessary,
# and performs parallel copy operations.

# ... (file list and directory definitions) ...

NOT_COPIED_FILES=()

while (( ${#FILES[@]} )); do
  SOURCE_FILES=( "${FILES[@]/#/${SOURCE_DIR}/}" )
  TOTAL_SIZE=$(du -sbc "${SOURCE_FILES[@]}" | awk 'END{print $1}')
  AVAILABLE_SPACE=$(df --portability --block-size=1 "$TARGET_DIR" | awk 'END{print $4}')

  if (( TOTAL_SIZE <= AVAILABLE_SPACE )); then
    printf 'Copying files... %s\n' "${FILES[@]}"
    echo "From ${SOURCE_DIR} -> ${TARGET_DIR}"

    for file in "${FILES[@]}"; do
      # Copy files in parallel
      cp -r "${SOURCE_DIR}/${file}" "${TARGET_DIR}/" &
    done
    break
  else
    # Remove the largest file if not enough space
    NOT_COPIED_FILES+=("${FILES[-1]}")
    unset 'FILES[-1]'
  fi
done

printf 'No room left on ssd for: %s\n' "${NOT_COPIED_FILES[@]}"
wait # Wait for all background copy processes to complete
```

The AlphaFold 3 repository includes a script for efficiently copying large biological sequence files to local Solid State Drives \(SSDs\), particularly within a Google Cloud Platform environment\. This process is managed by the [`src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh) script, which aims to optimize data transfer by prioritizing files to fit within available storage space and parallelizing copy operations\. The script dynamically assesses the total size of files slated for transfer against the available space on the target SSD\. If the total size exceeds the available capacity, it intelligently prunes the list of files to be copied, ensuring that as much data as possible is transferred\. Files that cannot be accommodated due to space constraints are identified and reported\. This approach supports efficient data staging for downstream processing, especially when dealing with extensive biological datasets where local storage performance is critical\. The script also leverages parallel execution to expedite the copying process, enhancing overall throughput\.## Legal and Licensing Information

The legal framework governing the use of AlphaFold 3 model parameters and outputs is detailed in the [`legal`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/legal) directory, alongside the primary policy documents [`WEIGHTS_PROHIBITED_USE_POLICY.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/WEIGHTS_PROHIBITED_USE_POLICY.md) and [`WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md)\. These documents outline the terms of use, prohibited usage policies, non\-commercial use restrictions, attribution requirements, and limitations on distribution and training of derivative models\.

 AlphaFold 3's model parameters and outputs are strictly designated for non\-commercial use by non\-commercial organizations such as universities, non\-profits, and research institutes\. Commercial activities, or research conducted on behalf of commercial entities, are explicitly prohibited\. The core policy [`WEIGHTS_PROHIBITED_USE_POLICY.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/WEIGHTS_PROHIBITED_USE_POLICY.md) details specific restrictions, including the prohibition against using AlphaFold 3 outputs to train or create derivative machine learning models for biomolecular structure prediction\. This policy also forbids using the assets to misinform, misrepresent, or engage in dangerous, illegal, or malicious activities\. Furthermore, it prohibits the distribution of outputs without proper notice, which must include a clear reference to the [README\.md?plain=1 L3](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/README.md?plain=1#L3) and a specific legally binding text\.

 Attribution is a mandatory requirement for all AlphaFold 3 outputs\. Users must cite the scientific article "Abramson, J et al\. Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3\. *Nature* \(2024\)" when distributing outputs or disclosing findings\. The distribution of model parameters is highly restricted; they are considered confidential information and may only be shared internally within an organization by authorized personnel\. Attempts to circumvent these access restrictions are explicitly prohibited\.

 The [`WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/85c4d20505fd5cef05eac22b534d4e793971ae69/WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md) document further clarifies the intellectual property rights, disclaimers, and liabilities\. It grants a non\-exclusive, royalty\-free, revocable, non\-transferable license for accessing, using, and modifying AlphaFold 3 assets, conditional on adherence to these terms and the prohibited use policy\. Crucially, AlphaFold 3 and its outputs are provided "as is," without warranties, and are not intended or validated for clinical use or medical advice\. Users bear sole responsibility for their use and distribution of the outputs, and Google's liability is limited\. Disputes are governed by California law, with resolution typically occurring in Santa Clara County courts\. These legal documents are provided in multiple languages, including Bahasa Indonesia, Latin American Spanish, Canadian French, and Brazilian Portuguese, to ensure broad accessibility and compliance\.### Non\-Commercial Use and Prohibited Activities
